findings.text: This lane shows two shapes of the tick programming operation: a header inline that always reports success without touching hardware, and a one shot implementation that stops the device on a far future deadline, ensures one shot mode when resuming from stopped, then delegates to the generic program routine.

Clock event control exposes a state switch operation that only acts on change and a program operation that records the requested deadline and drives coupled, high resolution timer, or tick count programming paths.

Timekeeping exposes a monotonic now query built from a base plus scaled cycle delta and an expiry to cycle conversion that only succeeds when the requested source identity matches the installed source.

Next deadline selection ignores soft bases once the soft interrupt is already active, otherwise refreshes the recorded soft deadline, then compares the earliest hard deadline against the soft deadline and adopts the soft timer and soft time when soft is earlier.

Scanning for the earliest deadline walks only the bases marked active under the requested soft or hard mask, adjusts each base deadline by its offset, keeps the smallest non negative value with default far future, and remembers the associated queued timer separately for soft and hard groups.

Hardware reprogramming always updates the stored next deadline first, then skips touching the device when high resolution mode is inactive under configuration and per cpu flag, when a hang was previously flagged to let the system progress, or when the caller asked to skip equal values and nothing changed.

Reprogramming for a single timer normalizes its deadline by base offset with negative results clamped to immediate, updates remote soft tracking only when not already activated and the new time is earlier than stored, honors a reprogram permission flag, and never programs another processor device, an equal or later deadline, or a pending deferred rearm.

Starting a timer validates soft versus hard mode against timer character, resolves relative deadlines against the base clock with low resolution compensation, prefers keeping the timer on its base to avoid double device updates, suppresses programming under deferred rearm while marking need for later update, kicks a remote processor only when the local base is offline and the timer is first, and applies a lazy optimization that avoids reprogramming when the new deadline is not before the armed time.

Generic event programming rejects negative deadlines, records the request even when the device is shut down without further action, expects one shot state, routes high resolution timer feature devices through a dedicated time based callback and coupled devices through a cycle conversion path, then programs tick counts clamped to device limits with overdue handling that only fails when not forced and a minimum tick fallback that sets a forced marker.

Minimum delta recovery re bases the deadline on current time plus the device minimum, counts retries, either retries indefinitely with growth after repeated failures or accumulates over a bounded number of attempts, returns immediately without error when shut down, and grows small minima to a floor and larger ones by half up to a global limit with warnings and a far future deadline once the limit is reached.

Monotonic time is read under a sequence protected snapshot of base and cycle state, converting the masked cycle delta since the last update with scale and accumulated remainder, using an inlined source read when available or a callback otherwise, and diverting oversized deltas to a backward motion guard or a safe wide multiply path.

Absolute to cycle conversion first does a racy identity precheck to avoid snapshot cost, then snapshots base cycles, base time, multiplier, shift and maximum span under sequence protection, aborts if identity changed, clamps the delta between zero and maximum, scales to cycles and adds the base cycles.
Next event scanning requires the per processor timer base lock to be held, and the matching unlock helper releases that same lock with interrupt state restore.

Both the monotonic now query and the expiry to cycle conversion take a sequence begin snapshot of timekeeper state and retry while the sequence indicates concurrent update, revalidating source identity inside the protected region for conversion.

The per processor timer aggregate carries a lock, online and activation flags for soft interrupt handling and high resolution mode, hang and deferred rearm markers, active base mask, stored soft and overall deadlines with associated next timer pointers, an array of per clock bases, and processor identity with cross call state for remote wakeup. Noted fields include lock and online and softirq_activated and hres_active and hang_detected and deferred_rearm and active_bases and softirq_expires_next and softirq_next_timer and next_timer and expires_next and cpu.

A clock base holds its own next deadline, a monotonic offset used to normalize deadlines, a queue of active timers whose first element yields the base next timer through container linkage, and a back pointer to the owning per processor base, while a timer carries its base pointer plus soft and hard and lazy and pinned character flags. Noted names include expires_next and offset and active and base and is_soft and is_hard and is_lazy and node.

A clock event device carries feature capability bits, a state field accessed only through helpers, callbacks for shutdown and mode entry plus next tick and next time programming, timing parameters for multiplier shift and minimum and maximum deltas in both time and tick units, the last programmed deadline with a forced marker, retry accounting, identity and name for coupled operation and diagnostics. Noted names include state_use_accessors and features and mult and shift and min_delta_ns and max_delta_ns and min_delta_ticks and next_event and next_event_forced and retries and cs_id and name.

Timekeeper read state comprises a clock pointer with mask and last cycle count, scaling multiplier and shift, accumulated sub second remainder, monotonic base time, source identity with reverse conversion multiplier shift and maximum span, guarded by a global sequence counter and a suspended flag. Noted names include clock and mask and cycle_last and mult and shift and xtime_nsec and base and cs_id and max_cycles.

The device moves among detached, shutdown, periodic, one shot and stopped one shot states: dummy devices accept any request without action, every transition clears the forced marker, detached and shutdown share the shutdown callback, periodic and one shot require matching capability and invoke their callbacks, and entry to stopped one shot requires already being in one shot and a dedicated callback when present.

Timer start reports whether hardware needs no update, needs an update because a newly first timer was queued, or needs a forced re evaluation because the previous first timer stayed local through removal and enqueue, with deferred rearm collapsing all cases to no immediate update while recording that an update is needed.

The hardware rearm path flows from stored deadline update through a trace and tick program call into generic clock event programming, providing the single funnel for high resolution timer hardware updates in this lane.
Monotonic now and expiry conversion serve as the time base entries for relative timer calculation, overdue detection, and coupled programming in this lane.

Hazards include warning on negative deadlines and on starting a timer while timekeeping is suspended, repairing a zero one shot multiplier to avoid a faulty scale, blocking hardware updates while a hang marker persists to preserve progress, treating minimum reprogramming failures by raising the minimum up to abandonment, and masking backward or overflowing cycle deltas to avoid time going backward.

A distinguished maximum time value denotes no pending event: next event scans default to it, tick programming stops the device on it, and minimum growth abandonment records it as the deadline. The name observed for this sentinel is KTIME_MAX.

Behavior is parameterized by soft versus hard activity masks, clock event state and feature families, timer mode bits for relative pinned soft and hard placement, start outcome hints for none versus reprogram versus forced reprogram, and negative error results for unsupported operation invalid argument and expired deadline.
